source.check: returned unopposed: no nomination was received (Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1933: 'No nominations were received for the County Electoral Divisions of Ahoghill, Ballycastle and Ballyclare. The present members for these divisions were deemed to be re-elected')

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received by Alexander Millar at the County Courthouse, Belfast, on 3 May 1933, withdrawals to 10 May, and a poll, if necessary, on Thursday 1 June 1933 (Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1933, p. 11: 'If a poll is necessary it will be taken on 1st June'). The only threatened contest, in Slemish, ended on 10 May when Robert Gregg withdrew, leaving John G. Wallace returned unopposed (Irish News, 11 May 1933, p. 4), so no poll was held in the county. No party labels were printed. Deemed re-elected; named in the News-Letter's report. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
